subject: Claude CCAF: Claude Code Configuration & Workflows
chapter: 3.6 Claude Code in CI/CD & Enterprise Deployment
description: Non-interactive mode (-p), GitHub Actions, corporate proxies, Zero Data Retention (ZDR), and OpenTelemetry chargeback.

questions.question: A CI script runs claude 'Analyze this PR for security issues' and hangs indefinitely waiting for interactive input. Correct fix?
options: Add the -p flag: claude -p 'Analyze this PR for security issues'
questions.answer: Add the -p flag: claude -p 'Analyze this PR for security issues'
questions.source: UD3-039 | Claude Code CLI reference — -p · GitHub Actions
questions.explanation: -p (print / non-interactive mode) runs Claude Code headlessly, outputting results directly to stdout and exiting without prompting for interactive input.

questions.question: CI runs behave inconsistently versus local runs because developers have different CLAUDE.md files, skills, and MCP servers. What ensures consistent CI execution?
options: Using the --bare flag, which skips auto-discovery of all local configuration (hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, CLAUDE.md).
Storing all developer configurations in version control and loading them in CI.
Running CI jobs on standardized Docker containers with identical configurations.
questions.answer: Using the --bare flag, which skips auto-discovery of all local configuration (hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, CLAUDE.md).
questions.source: UD2-039 | Claude Code CLI reference · Settings
questions.explanation: --bare skips auto-discovery of local hooks, skills, and memory files, providing an isolated, deterministic execution baseline in CI.
questions.examTrick: Deterministic CI baseline = --bare flag to disable local auto-discovery.
